easy.def: A word that shows what something belongs to or holds.
examples: I want a cup of milk.
This is a picture of my dog.
She is part of the team.

more.def: A word used to show that something belongs to a group, comes from somewhere, or tells the amount or type.
examples: A flock of geese flew over the lake.
The top of the mountain was covered in snow.
He is the youngest of four children.

easy.def: Away from a place, or not on.
examples: The cat jumped off.
Turn off the light.
She took her hat off.

more.def: Away from a place or a surface, or not turned on.
examples: The ball rolled off the table and bounced across the floor.
Please turn off the TV before bed.
He took off his muddy boots at the door.

easy.def: To make someone feel hurt or upset.
examples: I did not mean to offend you.
The joke offended her.
His words offended me.

more.def: To hurt someone's feelings or make them upset.
examples: Teasing a friend can offend them even if you mean it as a joke.
Her rude joke offended the class.
He was offended when no one thanked him.
I meant no offense.
His joke caused offense.
She took offense.

more.def: A feeling of being hurt or upset, or something that causes it.
examples: I meant no offense by my joke.
She took offense at the rude remark.
His words caused offense.

easy.def: The team that tries to score in a game.
examples: The offense scored a goal.
Our offense is strong.
The offense moved up the field.

more.def: The team or players who try to score in a sport.
examples: Our offense scored two goals.
The offense moved the ball down the field.
The coach told the offense to run faster.
The joke was offensive.
An offensive word.
The picture was offensive.

more.def: Causing hurt feelings or anger because it is rude.
examples: The joke was offensive and made her sad.
He apologized for his offensive remark.
The smell from the dump was offensive.

easy.def: To say you will give or do something.
examples: I offer you a cookie.
She offered me a seat.
He offered to help.

more.def: To say that you will give something or do something for someone if they want it.
examples: She offered to carry my backpack.
The shop offers free cookies to kids.
He offered me a seat on the bus.

easy.def: Something you say you will give or do.
examples: Thank you for your offer.
I took the offer of a ride.
The offer of free lunch was kind.

more.def: Something that you say you will give or do for someone.
examples: We accepted her offer to walk the dog.
The shop made an offer: buy one, get one free.
Thank you for your kind offer of help.
It was an offhand remark.
An offhand answer.
He was offhand.

more.def: Said or done casually without much thought.
examples: It was just an offhand remark.
He gave an offhand answer.
She was offhand about the prize.

easy.def: A room or building where people work at desks.
examples: Mom works in an office.
The school has an office.
I went to the office.

more.def: A room or building where people do desk work, or where a service is given.
examples: My dad works in an office on the tenth floor.
The school office is where you check in if you are late.
We stopped at the post office to mail the letter.

easy.def: A person who works for the police.
examples: The officer helped us cross.
An officer waved to us.
The officer found the lost dog.

more.def: A person who works for the police, often wearing a uniform.
examples: A police officer helped the children find their way.
The officer directed traffic outside the school.
An officer returned the lost bike to its owner.

easy.def: A leader in the army or navy.
examples: The officer gave an order.
An officer on the ship looked at the map.
The army officer led the group.

more.def: A person who has a position of authority in the army, navy or other group.
examples: The ship's officer checked the map before turning.
Each officer in the army leads a group of soldiers.
She became an officer in the navy.
The official rules.
It is official.
An official letter.

more.def: Approved by people in charge, or coming from them.
examples: The official rules are posted on the wall.
It's official: school is closed.
She received an official letter from the mayor.
The official blew the whistle.
The city official spoke.
A game official.

more.def: A person who holds a position of authority.
examples: The official blew the whistle to start the game.
A city official spoke at the meeting.
The officials checked the scores.
The park is officially open.
He was officially named captain.
The game is officially over.

more.def: In a way that is formal and approved by someone in charge.
examples: The winter season officially begins in December.
He was officially named captain of the team.
The mayor officially opened the new bridge.

easy.def: In the sea, away from the shore.
examples: An offshore wind blew.
The offshore island.
The oil rig is offshore.

more.def: Located or happening in the sea, a little way from the shore.
examples: The offshore wind blew the sand and the boats out to sea.
The oil company built an offshore platform in the deep water.
We could see an offshore island in the distance.

easy.def: Out at sea, away from land.
examples: The ship anchored offshore.
Whales swim offshore.
We sailed offshore.

more.def: Away from the shore and out in the sea.
examples: The ship anchored offshore until the storm passed.
Whales swim offshore, far from the beach.
The fishing boat went two miles offshore.

easy.def: The young of a person or animal.
examples: The mother and her offspring.
A bear and its offspring.
The offspring is small.

more.def: The young of a person, an animal or a plant, such as children or the babies of an animal.
examples: The mother bear protected her offspring from danger.
Rabbits can have many offspring in one year.
The tree's offspring grew as small seedlings beside it.
I often play outside.
We often go to the park.
It often rains here.
My grandmother often tells stories about her childhood.
It often snows here in January.
We often ride bikes after school.
